items.title: Joe Muranyi interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: I had like one lesson or something or two lessons, and he was letting me hold it and things like that

ctx.x: Oh you mean you were taking lessons and you never even got to play one for a while.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. I don’t remember if I had solfeggio or singing, maybe, but it was grand staff, the do-re-me-fa-so-la-C and all that kind of stuff, and I guess I sort of forgot it because — I don’t know, maybe it had some early — and then I was going to take violin lessons. There was a guy named Pragia who came from Cleveland. And I don’t think he was a gypsy, he was just sort of a very artistic, very, a fairly young guy with pale skin and very delicate fingers and was a hell of a violin player. And I had like…
That’s true. So what was the first sort of jazz-related music that caught your ear?
